title: Extension-by-zero colimit of a strict system of local quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\lambda$ be a set-sized ordinal, and let $(U_\alpha)_{\alpha<\lambda}$ be an increasing open cover of $X$. For each $\alpha$ let $I_\alpha$ be an unbounded cochain complex of $\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] $f_{\beta\alpha}:I_\beta\to I_\alpha|_{U_\beta}$ are given for $\beta<\alpha<\lambda$, satisfying $f_{\gamma\alpha}=(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{U_\gamma})\circ f_{\gamma\beta}$ as chain maps whenever $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$. Write $j_\alpha:U_\alpha\hookrightarrow X$ and use normalized extension by zero $j_{\alpha,!}$ and its adjunction unit $\eta_\alpha:I_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}(j_{\alpha,!}I_\alpha)|_{U_\alpha}$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-extension-by-zero-adjunction], applied termwise. For $\beta<\alpha$ let $T_{\beta\alpha}:j_{\beta,!}I_\beta\to j_{\alpha,!}I_\alpha$ be the degreewise adjoint of $(\eta_\alpha|_{U_\beta})\circ f_{\beta\alpha}$. These are chain maps and satisfy $T_{\gamma\alpha}=T_{\beta\alpha}\circ T_{\gamma\beta}$. Their termwise colimit $L=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\lambda}j_{\alpha,!}I_\alpha$ exists as a cochain complex [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If $c_\alpha:j_{\alpha,!}I_\alpha\to L$ are its coprojections, then $s_\alpha=(c_\alpha|_{U_\alpha})\circ\eta_\alpha:I_\alpha\to L|_{U_\alpha}$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $s_\beta=(s_\alpha|_{U_\beta})\circ f_{\beta\alpha}$ as chain maps for every $\beta<\alpha$. Consequently $Q(s_\alpha):QI_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}(QL)|_{U_\alpha}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{U_\alpha})$ [def-pc-derived-category], where $Q$ denotes passage to the derived category. No continuity of the open cover at limit indices, no K-injectivity, and no negative-Hom vanishing are assumed.

proof.text:
Put $D_\alpha=j_{\alpha,!}I_\alpha$ and abbreviate restriction by $R_\beta$. The adjunction bijection sends $T_{\beta\alpha}$ to $R_\beta(T_{\beta\alpha})\eta_\beta=R_\beta(\eta_\alpha)f_{\beta\alpha}$. Since extension by zero is additive, the adjuncts of $d_{D_\alpha}T_{\beta\alpha}$ and $T_{\beta\alpha}d_{D_\beta}$ agree: naturality of $\eta_\alpha$ moves the differential through the unit, and $d f_{\beta\alpha}=f_{\beta\alpha}d$. Injectivity of the bijection makes $T_{\beta\alpha}$ a chain map. For $\gamma<\beta<\alpha$, the adjunct of $T_{\beta\alpha}T_{\gamma\beta}$ is
$$R_\gamma(T_{\beta\alpha})R_\gamma(\eta_\beta)f_{\gamma\beta}=R_\gamma(\eta_\alpha)(f_{\beta\alpha}|_{U_\gamma})f_{\gamma\beta}=R_\gamma(\eta_\alpha)f_{\gamma\alpha}.$$
Thus it equals $T_{\gamma\alpha}$. Add identity transitions to obtain a diagram indexed by the small ordinal $\lambda$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, label lemma-glueing-increasing-union, proof: termwise extension-by-zero colimit, stalk display, and final colimit on X.

proof.text: The small Zariski opens site has sheafification, so the module-sheaf colimit theorem gives $L^n=\operatorname{colim}_\alpha D_\alpha^n$ in every integer degree. Define $d_L^n$ by $d_L^n c_\alpha^n=c_\alpha^{n+1}d_{D_\alpha}^n$. Compatibility follows from Step 1. The composites $d_L^{n+1}d_L^n$ and zero agree after every coprojection and hence agree by colimit uniqueness. The $c_\alpha$ are chain maps. A compatible family of chain maps out of the $D_\alpha$ factors degreewise uniquely through $L$; the resulting maps commute with differentials because this can again be checked after every coprojection. Thus this is also a colimit in complexes. This construction includes $\lambda=0$; the cover then forces $X=\varnothing$, and all assertions indexed by $\alpha$ are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, termwise colimit; Modules on Sites Tag 03DB, label lemma-limits-colimits, existence of module-sheaf colimits.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha<\lambda$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, so $\lambda$ is nonempty. Its ordinal order is filtered: the larger of two indices receives both arrows and there are no distinct parallel arrows. Filtered colimits of module sheaves are exact by the first assertion of [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor], applied to the small Zariski opens site and $\mathcal O_X$. Apply [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] to this abelian category, this index category and the cochain shape on $\mathbf Z$. By Step 2 its conclusion says that the maps $H^q(c_\beta)$ exhibit $H^q(L)$ as the colimit of $H^q(D_\beta)$, for all $\beta<\lambda$. There is no bound on the complexes or on $q$.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, stalk display and exact filtered-colimit argument; Modules on Sites Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), exactness; the exact-colimit homology statement is also the three-term calculation of Algebra Tag 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact).

proof.text:
Fix $x\in U_\alpha$. Stalk preservation of filtered colimits applied to the cocone in Step 3 gives
$$H^q(L)_x\cong\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}H^q(D_\beta)_x,$$
with legs $H^q(c_\beta)_x$. Kernels, images and cokernels commute with stalks, so the formula $H^q(K)=\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ gives natural identifications $H^q(K)_x\cong H^q(K_x)$. For $\beta\ge\alpha$, we have $x\in U_\beta$; the inside-stalk isomorphism of extension by zero identifies $(D_\beta)_x$ with $(I_\beta)_x$. By the adjunction formula the unit is $\eta_\beta=\theta_{I_\beta}|_{U_\beta}$, so its stalk at any $y\in U_\beta$ is this inside-stalk isomorphism; by the stalk criterion on $U_\beta$ each $\eta_\beta$ is an isomorphism, as written in the statement. The adjunction formula from Step 1 identifies $(T_{\beta\delta})_x$ with $(f_{\beta\delta})_x$ for $\alpha\le\beta<\delta$. Since $f_{\beta\delta}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, exactness of stalks makes all corresponding maps $H^q(D_\beta)_x\to H^q(D_\delta)_x$ isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, label lemma-glueing-increasing-union, proof: termwise extension-by-zero colimit, stalk display, and final colimit on X.

proof.text: Removing indices below $\alpha$ does not change the colimit in Step 4. Explicitly, any cocone $(m_\beta)_{\beta\ge\alpha}$ on the tail extends to the whole diagram by setting $m_\gamma=m_{\max(\alpha,\gamma)}H^q(T_{\gamma,\max(\alpha,\gamma)})_x$, with identity transitions when the indices coincide. Step 1 proves the cocone identities, and every extension is forced by the arrow $\gamma\to\max(\alpha,\gamma)$. Thus restriction and extension of cocones are inverse, preserving the vertex and its morphisms; the universal property gives the asserted unchanged colimit and its legs.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, label lemma-glueing-increasing-union, proof: termwise extension-by-zero colimit, stalk display, and final colimit on X.

proof.text: Write $M_\beta=H^q(D_\beta)_x$ on this tail, and $u_{\beta\delta}:M_\beta\to M_\delta$ for its isomorphism transitions. The maps $u_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}:M_\beta\to M_\alpha$ form a cocone since $u_{\alpha\delta}=u_{\beta\delta}u_{\alpha\beta}$. They induce $v:\operatorname{colim}_{\beta\ge\alpha}M_\beta\to M_\alpha$. If $k_\beta$ are its colimit legs, then $vk_\alpha=1$, and $k_\alpha v k_\beta=k_\alpha u_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}=k_\beta$, hence $k_\alpha v=1$. Therefore the $\alpha$ leg is an isomorphism. Under Steps 4--5 and the unit identification this leg is precisely $H^q(s_\alpha)_x$. This holds for every $x\in U_\alpha$ and integer $q$. The stalk criterion for module-sheaf isomorphisms makes every $H^q(s_\alpha)$ an isomorphism; hence $s_\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D6B, label lemma-glueing-increasing-union, proof: termwise extension-by-zero colimit, stalk display, and final colimit on X.

proof.text:
For $\beta<\alpha$, the cocone identity and the adjunct formula give the chain-map equality
$$s_\beta=R_\beta(c_\beta)\eta_\beta=R_\beta(c_\alpha)R_\beta(T_{\beta\alpha})\eta_\beta=R_\beta(c_\alpha)R_\beta(\eta_\alpha)f_{\beta\alpha}=(s_\alpha|_{U_\beta})f_{\beta\alpha}.$$
Restriction is exact, so it commutes with kernels and cokernels and therefore preserves quasi-isomorphisms; it consequently descends to the derived localizations. By the definition of these localizations $Q(s_\alpha)$ is invertible, with target $Q(L|_{U_\alpha})=(QL)|_{U_\alpha}$. This proves the derived assertion. The proof used only strict composition, the unit, and exact filtered colimits; no continuity condition on the cover, K-injectivity or negative-Hom vanishing entered.
